As Reuters reports, the Munich Regional Court ruled on Friday (31st July) that Suno does not have the right to train its AI systems on music represented by German music collection society GEMA, who brought the case against the company last year. GEMA represents around 95,000 rightsholders in Germany and over two million worldwide. At a hearing in March, GEMA provided evidence that AI-generated music created using Suno closely matched multiple copyrighted compositions in melody, harmony and rhythm. articles.title: BBC Radio 6 Music to celebrate Black British dance music with new show, Rave Forever
articles.excerpt: A new weekly show dedicated to Black British dance music is coming to BBC Radio 6 Music. Beginning this Friday (7th August), Rave Forever will be broadcast all day (7AM–7PM) every Friday this month as part of the BBC’s The Music is Black season, in collaboration with V&A East Museum’s The Music is Black: A British Story exhibition. Each week will focus on a different decade, kicking off with the '80s before heading into the '90s (14th August), '00s (21st August), and '10s (28th August). Alongside historic trips into the likes of lovers rock, reggae, jungle, drum & bass, trip-hop, UK funky, UKG and grime, the final segment of the show will feature 30-minute guest mixes or playlists.
